_comment: This file lists the kinds of file a Vita project can hold. Chimera's New Project window is built from it. A project is one game, the licence a packaged game needs, and optionally what the game already saved. The system software is given as firmware, and the System Software setting says which parts.

slots.title: Game
slots.help: The game, in one of three forms. It can be a .vpk file. It can be a NoNpDRM dump packed as a .zip (the game's folder, including its sce_sys/package/work.bin). Or it can be a PlayStation Store package (.pkg), with the game's licence in the Licence slot. Vita3K installs it into the machine before it starts. Vita3K's compatibility list (vita3k.org/compatibility) says which games work.

slots.title: Licence
slots.help: The licence that decrypts a .pkg game. It is either the game's work.bin (the 512-byte file a NoNpDRM dump keeps in sce_sys/package) or the console's own .rif file for the game. A package is encrypted and installs nothing without it. A .vpk or a .zip dump needs none, because a dump includes its own. The project and the movie record exactly which file was used, as they do for the game.

slots.title: Save data
slots.help: What the game already saved, as Emulator > Export Save Data... wrote it. It is a .zip with savedata/<TITLE ID>/... (the system's save data) and data/... (where homebrew keeps its files). A save copied from a Vita with ux0:/user/00/ in front of the path, or a plain <TITLE ID>/ folder, is accepted too. It is put into the machine before the game starts.
